About Me

Bridging computation
& living systems

I am a final-year Biomedical Engineering student at Islamic University, Kushtia, with research spanning computational cancer biology and functional biomaterials for wound healing.

I have co-authored research published in Computers in Biology and Medicine and Computational Biology and Chemistry (Elsevier), and presented at IEEE CS BDC Summer Symposium 2025 and IEEE COMPAS 2025. Three additional manuscripts are under review.

My final-year project (2026) focuses on the development and characterization of doxorubicin-loaded chitosan–xanthan gum nanoparticles for pH-responsive breast cancer drug delivery — engineering a biodegradable polyelectrolyte nanocarrier that releases its payload preferentially in the acidic tumour microenvironment.

Beyond research, I pursue Nazrul Geeti, classical dance, and aquascaping. These creative interests have strengthened my patience, observation, and discipline while balancing intensive academic research.

Research Interests

Areas of Focus

🧵
Biomaterials & Tissue Engineering

Electrospun scaffolds and smart wound dressings with stimuli-responsive behavior. Hands-on cell culture experience from internship at HGRTC, Dhaka, and the IU Biomedical Research Center.

🧬
Computational Drug Discovery

In-silico approaches including molecular docking, MD simulation, and ADMET profiling to identify and validate small-molecule inhibitors against cancer-driving protein targets such as ErbB2 and PARP1.

🔬
Cancer Biology

Targeting oncogenic signaling pathways — particularly HER2/ErbB2 and PARP1 — through in-silico and experimental approaches.

🩺
Wound Healing & Infection

Functional biomaterial solutions for chronic wound management, specifically diabetic foot ulcers with antibiofilm and antioxidant properties.

💊
Nanoparticle Drug Delivery

Polysaccharide-based nanocarriers — chitosan–xanthan gum polyelectrolyte complexes — engineered for pH-responsive, tumour-targeted release of chemotherapeutics such as doxorubicin, with controlled particle size, encapsulation efficiency, and sustained release kinetics.

⚛️
Medical Physics

Clinical exposure to PET-CT, LINAC radiotherapy, and cyclotron radiopharmaceuticals through structured training at BAEC/INMP.

Research Focus

Current & Ongoing Projects

★ Final Year Project · 2026
Development and Characterization of Doxorubicin-Loaded Chitosan–Xanthan Gum Nanoparticles for pH-Responsive Breast Cancer Drug Delivery

Chitosan–xanthan gum polyelectrolyte nanoparticles loaded with doxorubicin, prepared by ionic gelation and characterized for size, zeta potential, and encapsulation efficiency. Designed to release the drug preferentially at tumour-acidic pH 5.0 over physiological pH 7.4.

ChitosanXanthan GumDoxorubicinNanoparticlesIonic GelationpH-Responsive ReleaseBreast CancerDLS · FTIR · SEMMTT Assay
🩹
Work in Progress
Janus Electrospun PCL/Chitosan-Gelatin-Gum Arabic Nanofibrous Membrane Loaded with Computationally Screened Protocatechuic Acid from Phyllanthus emblica for Chronic Wound Microenvironment Modulation

Asymmetric electrospun bilayer pairing a hydrophobic PCL barrier with a chitosan–gelatin–gum arabic bioactive layer, loaded with protocatechuic acid identified by computational screening of Phyllanthus emblica phytochemicals — designed to modulate the chronic wound microenvironment through antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial action.

ElectrospinningJanus MembraneChitosan · Gum ArabicProtocatechuic AcidPhyllanthus emblicaVirtual ScreeningChronic Wound
🧬
Published Research Article
Computational Targeting of ErbB2 Homodimer in Breast Cancer

Molecular docking, ADMET profiling, and MD simulation evaluating N-Carbobenzoxy-L-Phenylalanine as a disruptor of ErbB2 homodimer signaling in HER2-positive breast cancer.
